clauses.reason: Operative as the amending command whose substituted section 2 remains the text of EO 10717. The authority recital and the command to substitute sections 2, 7 and 8 were carried out on signing; the held 5 U.S.C. 4504 note prints EO 10717 as amended by this order and still carries the substituted section 2, while sections 7 and 8 as substituted were later deleted by EO 12014 (see their own clauses). EO 12014 is attached as a later event because it undid part of what the lead substituted.

clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 2(a) states that the President presents the award to civilian officers or employees for the best achievements having current impact, and lists four exemplifying qualities. The held current Code note prints section 2(a) of EO 10717 word for word as substituted here; no later instrument touches section 2.

clauses.current_legal_basis: Continuing: the held 5 U.S.C. 4504 note (release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09) prints section 2(b) of EO 10717 in the same words; no held instrument amends or revokes it.
clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 2(b) requires the importance of the achievements to be so outstanding that greater recognition than the agency head can give is deserved, generally limits awards to five a year and leaves the timing to the President. The held current Code note prints it in the same words.

later_events.mechanism: amendment of the parent Executive Order 10717 by deleting its sections 3 through 9 (including sections 7 and 8 as substituted by this order) and abolishing the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board

clauses.mechanism: express amendment by deletion: EO 12014 abolished the Board and deleted sections 3 through 9 of EO 10717, including section 7 as substituted by this order
clauses.reason: Ended by EO 12014 on 1977-10-19. Section 7 authorized the Board to prescribe nomination forms and barred it from recommending a nominee without the concurrence of the head of the employing agency. EO 12014 abolished the Board and amended EO 10717 by deleting sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 and adding new sections 3 and 4; the nomination form and concurrence rule now sit in new section 4 for the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission, so this clause's command was ended by deletion and replaced elsewhere. EO 12014 states no separate effective date, so its signing date is used.

later_events.mechanism: amendment of the parent Executive Order 10717 by deleting its sections 3 through 9 (including sections 7 and 8 as substituted by this order) and abolishing the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board

clauses.mechanism: express amendment by deletion: EO 12014 abolished the Board and deleted sections 3 through 9 of EO 10717, including section 8 as substituted by this order
clauses.reason: Ended by EO 12014 on 1977-10-19. Section 8 required the Board to follow subsections (b) and (c) of section 304 of the Government Employees' Incentive Awards Act and its own criteria and made persons appointed by the President ineligible unless in the Board's opinion they served in a career position. EO 12014 abolished the Board and deleted section 8 together with sections 3 through 7 and 9; the career-position limit reappears in new section 4(c) with the Commission in place of the Board. EO 12014 states no separate effective date, so its signing date is used.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register original (26 FR 11937, PDF page 3) is Executive Order 10979, signed by John F. Kennedy on December 12, 1961, amending Executive Order 10717 of June 27, 1957 (the President's Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service) by substituting new sections 2, 7 and 8. The packet inventory lumped section 2(b), section 7 and section 8 into the last item clause; it is corrected by overrides into the lead, section 2(a), section 2(b), section 7 and section 8, because their fates differ. EO 12014 (October 19, 1977) abolished the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board and amended EO 10717 by deleting sections 3 through 9 and adding new sections 3 and 4; sections 7 and 8 (the Board's nomination form and its guidance) therefore ended on 1977-10-19, the nomination principles reappearing in new section 4 of EO 10717. Sections 2(a) and 2(b) were not touched: the held U.S. Code note under 5 U.S.C. 4504 (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints section 2(a)-(b) of EO 10717 in the same words as this order and shows EO 10717 as amended through EO 12107 with no ending.

savings.reason: EO 12014 deleted sections 7 and 8 and in the same sentence added new sections 3 and 4 of EO 10717 carrying the nomination procedure and the concurrence and career-position principles to the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission, so the functions were transferred rather than lost; no award made under the order is invalidated by either instrument.
